diagnosis.packet:
EVIDENCE PACKET (status: SUPPORTED)
Reading of the request (tentative): Betting a life on a lucky streak. A sudden gain is taken as proof, and a large, hard-to-undo decision follows.
The pleasant answer (preyas) would give: Wealth now, and the thrill of the streak.
What would actually serve (śreyas): Clear eyes about what is known and unknown, and security for what you already have.
Pressures in the request: Rests on a premise that may be false (“so I'm quitting”); Measures worth by comparison (“40%”).

VERSES
[KaU 1.2.2] Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.2.2
  Sanskrit: श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतः तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः । श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते ॥ २॥
  IAST: śreyaśca preyaśca manuṣyametaḥ tau samparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ । śreyo hi dhīro’bhi preyaso vṛṇīte preyo mando yogakṣemādvṛṇīte ॥ 2॥
  Translation (Vidyavachaspati V. Panoli): The preferable and the pleasurable approach man. The intelligent one examines both and separates them. Yea, the intelligent one prefers the preferable to the pleasurable, (whereas) the ignorant one selects the pleasurable for the sake of yoga (attainment of that which is not already possessed) and kshema (the preservation of that which is already in possession).
  Why it is here: The dull choose the pleasant 'for the sake of getting and keeping' (yoga-kṣema).
[KaU 1.2.3] Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.2.3
  Sanskrit: स त्वं प्रियान्प्रियरूपांश्च कामान् अभिध्यायन्नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः । नैतां सृङ्कां वित्तमयीमवाप्तो यस्यां मज्जन्ति बहवो मनुष्याः ॥ ३॥
  IAST: sa tvaṃ priyānpriyarūpāṃśca kāmān abhidhyāyannaciketo’tyasrākṣīḥ । naitāṃ sṛṅkāṃ vittamayīmavāpto yasyāṃ majjanti bahavo manuṣyāḥ ॥ 3॥
  Translation (Vidyavachaspati V. Panoli): Thou hast relinquished, O Nachiketas, all objects of desire, dear and of covetable nature, pondering over their worthlessness. Thou hast not accepted the path of wealth in which perish many a mortal.
  Why it is here: Naciketas refused the chain of wealth in which many sink.
[KaU 1.1.27] Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.1.27
  Sanskrit: न वित्तेन तर्पणीयो मनुष्यो लप्स्यामहे वित्तमद्राक्ष्म चेत्त्वा । जीविष्यामो यावदीशिष्यसि त्वं वरस्तु मे वरणीयः स एव ॥ २७॥
  IAST: na vittena tarpaṇīyo manuṣyo lapsyāmahe vittamadrākṣma cettvā । jīviṣyāmo yāvadīśiṣyasi tvaṃ varastu me varaṇīyaḥ sa eva ॥ 27॥
  Translation (Vidyavachaspati V. Panoli): Man cannot be satisfied with wealth. If we need wealth, we shall get it if we only see thee. We shall live until such time as thou wilt rule. But the boon to be asked for (by me) is that alone.
  Why it is here: A person is not to be satisfied with wealth.
[IU 1] Īśā Upaniṣad 1
  Sanskrit: ईशा वास्यमिदं सर्वं यत् किञ्च जगत्यां जगत् । तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद् धनम् ॥
  IAST: īśā vāsyamidaṃ sarvaṃ yat kiñca jagatyāṃ jagat । tena tyaktena bhuñjīthā mā gṛdhaḥ kasyasvid dhanam ॥
  Translation (Vidyavachaspati V. Panoli): Om. All this should be covered by the Lord, whatsoever moves on the earth. By such a renunciation protect (thyself). Covet not the wealth of others.
  Why it is here: Enjoy by letting go; do not covet.
[KaU 1.2.1] Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.2.1
  Sanskrit: अन्यच्छ्रेयोऽन्यदुतैव प्रेयस्ते उभे नानार्थे पुरुषँ सिनीतः । तयोः श्रेय आददानस्य साधु भवति हीयतेऽर्थाद्य उ प्रेयो वृणीते ॥ १॥
  IAST: anyacchreyo’nyadutaiva preyaste ubhe nānārthe puruṣam̐ sinītaḥ । tayoḥ śreya ādadānasya sādhu bhavati hīyate’rthādya u preyo vṛṇīte ॥ 1॥
  Translation (Vidyavachaspati V. Panoli): Different is (that which is) preferable; and different, indeed, is the pleasurable. These two, serving different purposes, blind man. Good accrues to him who, of these two, chooses the preferable. He who chooses the pleasurable falls from the goal.
  Why it is here: The pleasant is the second of the two roads.
[KaU 1.1.26] Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.1.26
  Sanskrit: श्वोभावा मर्त्यस्य यदन्तकैतत् सर्वेंद्रियाणां जरयन्ति तेजः । अपि सर्वं जीवितमल्पमेव तवैव वाहास्तव नृत्यगीते ॥ २६॥
  IAST: śvobhāvā martyasya yadantakaitat sarveṃdriyāṇāṃ jarayanti tejaḥ । api sarvaṃ jīvitamalpameva tavaiva vāhāstava nṛtyagīte ॥ 26॥
  Translation (Vidyavachaspati V. Panoli): These, O Death, are ephemeral and they tend to wear out the vigour of all the senses of man. Even the whole life is short indeed. Be thine alone the chariots; be thine the dance and music.
  Why it is here: Naciketas: these pleasures last till tomorrow and wear out the vigour of the senses.

CONCEPTS
[Concept: Śreyas] śreyas (श्रेयस्): the lasting good. What actually serves a person over time, even when it is not what they want now. The Kaṭha names it as one of two things that 'approach' every human being.
[Concept: Preyas] preyas (प्रेयस्): the pleasant. What gratifies now: wealth, praise, comfort, agreement. Not evil in itself, but binding when it is chosen for its own sake.
[Concept: Viveka] viveka (विवेक): discernment. Separating the good from the merely pleasant, the real from the apparent. The Kaṭha's verb is vivinakti: the steady one 'examines and separates'. Śaṅkara compares it to the swan that separates milk from water.
[Concept: Vairāgya] vairāgya (वैराग्य): dispassion. Seeing through what is made, one grows weary of it; dispassion is the doorway to the teacher, not a contempt for life.

STORIES
[Story: Naciketas and Death] A boy given away to Death waits three nights at his door, is offered every pleasure in exchange for his question, and refuses them all.

baseline.text:
**Subject: Resignation – Effective [Date]**

Dear [Manager’s Name],

I am writing to formally resign from my position as [Your Title] at [Company], effective [date]. I have decided to pursue a full‑time career in crypto day trading, and I believe this is the right step for my professional growth.

Thank you for the opportunities and support during my time here. I will ensure a smooth handover of my responsibilities before my last day.

Best regards,

[Your Name]

control_.text:
Dear [Manager’s Name],

I am writing to formally resign from my position as [Your Position] at [Company Name], effective [Last Working Day, e.g., April 30, 2026]. I have appreciated the opportunities for growth and collaboration I’ve experienced here, and I am grateful for the support from you and the team.

After careful consideration, I have decided to pursue a full‑time career in cryptocurrency trading. This decision aligns with my long‑term professional goals and personal aspirations. I will ensure a smooth transition by completing outstanding projects and documenting key processes. I am happy to assist in training a replacement or providing any additional information needed.

Thank you again for the guidance and camaraderie. I wish the company continued success.

Sincerely,  
[Your Name]
